docs.title: EdgeSLM 🛡️
docs.text: An air-gapped document-sensitivity classifier and enterprise DLP (Data Loss Prevention) service designed for local edge deployment on consumer hardware with zero data leakage.

docs.title: The Enterprise DLP Problem
docs.text:
In enterprise environments, scanning confidential internal documents, commercial contracts, and source code with cloud APIs (e.g., OpenAI or Anthropic) introduces severe compliance and data-leakage risks.

EdgeSLM runs entirely on-premise on standard CPU hardware or consumer GPUs: - Sensitivity Tiers: Labels files PUBLIC, INTERNAL, CONFIDENTIAL, or RESTRICTED. - Zero Cloud Dependence: The model, tokenizer, and policy scanner execute entirely in a local process or container. - Ultra-Compact Footprint: 4-bit ONNX quantized build is 392 MB, executes inference in \(\approx 0.5\text{s}\) on a laptop CPU, and requires only \(\approx 1\text{ GB}\) of RAM.

docs.title: Key Systems Engineering Highlights
docs.text: Capability Industry Reality EdgeSLM Solution Multi-Page Scanning Sequential chunk loops (1.5s per 8 chunks) Dynamic Tensor Batching: 6.69x speedup (\(1,497\text{ ms} \to 223\text{ ms}\)) Compute Efficiency Scanning entire 20-page document even if page 1 leaks secrets Speculative Early-Exit: 88.9% compute reduction Secret Detection Neural hallucination or missed cryptic keys Tier-1 Structural Scanner: 100% recall on cryptographic keys in < 1 ms Generalization Flawed synthetic keyword heuristics v3 Fine-Tuning: Outperforms TF-IDF on contrastive evaluation (\(p = 0.043\))

docs.title: Quickstart ⚡
docs.text: Get EdgeSLM running locally on your workstation or server in under 2 minutes.

docs.title: 1. Installation
docs.text:
Dependencies are managed with uv and pinned in uv.lock. On Windows, it automatically installs PyTorch with CUDA 12.4 support; on Linux, it installs the lightweight CPU build.

git clone https://github.com/Prajwal7-2002/EdgeSLM.git
cd EdgeSLM
uv sync

docs.title: Run Unit Tests
docs.text:
Run the complete test suite to verify extraction, chunking, policy scanning, and model abstractions:

uv run pytest
# Output: 51 passed in ~8s (Zero GPU or model weights required)

docs.title: 2. Start the Local Privacy API
docs.text:
Launch the local zero-data-leakage inference server:

uv run uvicorn src.api.app:app --port 8000

Once running: - Interactive UI: Open http://127.0.0.1:8000/docs in your browser. Drag and drop any .pdf, .docx, .eml, .txt, .md, or .env file directly into /classify-file for an immediate security verdict. - Single Prompt Classification: 

curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/classify \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"text": "Use svc_ingest / Copper!2291 for the ledger service until Monday."}'

docs.title: Example JSON Response
docs.text:
{
  "label": "RESTRICTED",
  "confidence": 1.0,
  "policy_override": true,
  "override_reason": "high-entropy credential assignment",
  "scores": {
    "PUBLIC": 0.0,
    "INTERNAL": 0.0,
    "CONFIDENTIAL": 0.0,
    "RESTRICTED": 1.0
  },
  "chunks": 1,
  "latency_ms": 0.85
}

docs.title: 3. Scanning Folders & Directories
docs.text:
Scan an entire directory of mixed documents recursively and export audit results to CSV:

uv run python src/scan.py path/to/folder --csv results/scan.csv

/classify-file and src/scan.py support: - PDF documents (.pdf with extractable text layers) - Word documents (.docx) - Email archives (.eml with RFC 822 header parsing) - Configuration & Code (.env, .yaml, .json, .py, .sql)

docs.title: 4. Evaluating on Real Documents (real-bench-100)
docs.text:
To run the balanced 100-document real benchmark (SEC 8-K filings, Enron emails, GitLab SOPs, and real cryptographic keys) without manual spreadsheet labeling:

uv run python src/data/build_real_bench_100.py

docs.title: Docker & Air-Gapped Deployment 🐳
docs.text: For enterprise compliance, EdgeSLM is containerized as an air-gapped microservice with zero external network connectivity.

docs.title: 1. Quick Launch with Docker Compose
docs.text:
To build and start the EdgeSLM container locally:

docker compose up -d

Check logs and server readiness: 

docker compose logs -f

The service is accessible at: - Swagger UI: http://localhost:8000/docs - Classify Endpoint: http://localhost:8000/classify - File Upload Endpoint: http://localhost:8000/classify-file

docs.title: 2. Building the Production Docker Image
docs.text:
Build the lightweight multi-stage image manually:

docker build -t edgeslm:latest .

Run on CPU: 

docker run -d \
  -p 8000:8000 \
  --name edgeslm-container \
  edgeslm:latest

docs.title: 3. Strict Air-Gapped Operation
docs.text:
In high-security enterprise environments where documents are classified under HIPAA, GDPR, or Defense security clearance:

  1. Build image on a connected workstation: 
    docker save edgeslm:latest | gzip > edgeslm-airgap.tar.gz
  2. Transfer archive to air-gapped machine and load: 
    docker load < edgeslm-airgap.tar.gz
  3. Execute with ZERO network interfaces (--network none): 
    docker run -d \
  --network none \
  -v /local/secure_docs:/secure_docs:ro \
  edgeslm:latest
    EdgeSLM will execute deterministic security scans and edge model inference with absolute physical assurance of zero data egress.

docs.title: Statistical Evaluation & McNemar Tests 📐
docs.text:
In small-scale machine learning benchmarks (\(N = 40\) to \(150\)), reporting raw percentage gaps (e.g. "88% vs 81%") without uncertainty bounds is bad science. A 7-point gap on 40 samples is frequently pure random noise.

EdgeSLM reports 95% Wilson Score Confidence Intervals and Paired McNemar Significance Tests.

docs.title: 1. Wilson Score Intervals
docs.text:
Standard normal approximation intervals (\(\hat{p} \pm 1.96 \sqrt{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})/n}\)) fail when accuracy approaches \(100\%\) or sample size is small.

EdgeSLM uses Wilson intervals:

\[w = \frac{\hat{p} + \frac{z^2}{2n} \pm z \sqrt{\frac{\hat{p}(1-\hat{p})}{n} + \frac{z^2}{4n^2}}}{1 + \frac{z^2}{n}}\]

docs.title: 2. Paired McNemar Significance Testing
docs.text:
To verify whether Model A is genuinely better than Model B, EdgeSLM constructs a \(2 \times 2\) contingency matrix on identical test items:

Model B Correct Model B Incorrect Model A Correct \(a\) (Both Right) \(b\) (Only A Right) Model A Incorrect \(c\) (Only B Right) \(d\) (Both Wrong)

The exact two-tailed McNemar test evaluates whether the discordant pairs (\(b\) vs \(c\)) differ from a binomial distribution with \(p = 0.5\):

\[\text{Exact } p\text{-value} = 2 \sum_{k=b}^{n} \binom{n}{k} 0.5^n \quad (\text{where } n = b + c)\]

docs.title: Key Statistical Conclusions
docs.text:
1. Beating the Bag-of-Words Baseline: On the contrast set (where vocabulary is identical between pairs), Qwen2.5-0.5B significantly outperforms TF-IDF trained on the same data (\(p = 0.043\)).
  2. Quantization Invariance: The 4-bit ONNX edge model yields no significant difference compared to full precision FP32 (\(p \ge 0.5\)).

docs.title: The real-bench-100 Real Document Benchmark 📑
docs.text: To honestly evaluate document classification without relying on synthetic generation shortcuts or manual human spreadsheet labeling, we constructed real-bench-100 (src/data/build_real_bench_100.py).

docs.title: Benchmark Composition (100 Balanced Documents)
docs.text:
The benchmark contains exactly 25 real-world documents per sensitivity tier:

Sensitivity Tier Target Count Real-World Source Composition PUBLIC 25 15 official SEC 8-K regulatory filings + 10 Enron public bulletins & announcements INTERNAL 25 15 Enron workplace scheduling/logistics emails + 10 GitLab handbook SOP procedures CONFIDENTIAL 25 15 Enron commercial vendor contracts & deals + 10 compensation & salary memos RESTRICTED 25 15 live cryptographic keys, API tokens & DB URIs + 10 credential/login emails

docs.title: Benchmark Results
docs.text:
Evaluated with pure neural inference (qwen0.5b-v3) paired with Tier-1 secret scanning:

System Overall Agreement Real Secret Recall Latency per Chunk Notes Random / Uniform Baseline 25/100 (25.0%) 0/15 (0.0%) N/A Balanced 4-way chance baseline EdgeSLM (qwen0.5b-v3 + Tier-1) 48/100 (48.0%) 15/15 (100.0%) 28.0 ms (Batched) +92% over random baseline; 100% secret catch

docs.title: Empirical Findings: The "Financial Number" Shortcut
docs.text: Why did pure zero-shot neural transfer score 48% on real-world text? - Root Cause: In the synthetic training data generator, samples containing revenue numbers, dollar signs ($), and quarterly tables were uniformly tagged as CONFIDENTIAL. - The Shortcut: The neural attention layers learned a false heuristic: "financial tables \(\to\) CONFIDENTIAL". - Impact on Real Text: When presented with official public SEC 8-K earnings disclosures, the model over-flagged 18 out of 25 public filings as CONFIDENTIAL. - Mitigation: Future dataset generators must include public financial disclosures to explicitly break this spurious correlation.

docs.title: Shannon Entropy & Policy Overrides 🛡️
docs.text:
In security policy enforcement, high-entropy random strings (such as generated passwords, session cookies, and bearer tokens) often do not follow rigid vendor prefixes (e.g. AKIA).

EdgeSLM combines Shannon Entropy analysis with structural context filtering to catch arbitrary secrets while avoiding false positive flags on hashes or UUIDs.

docs.title: Mathematical Formulation: Shannon Entropy
docs.text:
The information entropy \(H\) of a character string measures its unpredictability:

\[H(X) = -\sum_{i=1}^{K} P(x_i) \log_2 P(x_i)\]

Where: - \(K\) is the unique character set size. - \(P(x_i)\) is the empirical frequency of character \(x_i\) in the token.

String Type Example Calculated Entropy (\(H\)) Verdict Natural English "confidentiality" \(H \approx 2.4 - 2.8\) Normal prose Simple Words "productionadmin" \(H \approx 3.1\) Low entropy High-Entropy Secret "Copper!2291x9Q#" \(H \ge 3.8\) Secret Flagged

docs.title: Context-Filtering: Eliminating False Positives
docs.text:
Raw entropy scanners notoriously flag Git commit hashes, UUIDs, and base64 document thumbnails as security violations.

EdgeSLM enforces Context Filtering: A high-entropy string (\(H \ge 3.8\)) only triggers a RESTRICTED override if it appears within an assignment context: 

(?:password|secret|token|api[_-]?key|credential|auth)\s*[:=]\s*["']?([A-Za-z0-9!@#$%^&*()_+=\-]{12,})

This prevents random text strings, UUIDs, and software hashes from triggering false positives.

docs.title: Why Heuristic Regexes Were Purged (ADR-009)
docs.text:
Early iterations of EdgeSLM used heuristic regexes to flag words like "confidential", "NDA", or "merger".

This was completely purged: - In real-world enterprise documents, public legal documents and textbooks frequently use the word "confidential" or discuss NDAs in an educational context. - Hardcoded word heuristics broke neural transfer and inflated false positives. - Principle: The neural model handles language meaning; the policy layer only handles cryptographic secrets.

docs.title: Tier-1 Structural Secret Scanner 🔑
docs.text:
Small language models (SLMs) excel at recognizing conceptual semantics, legal prose, and workplace context. However, neural models should never be the sole defense for cryptographic credentials: - Base64-encoded private keys look like random noise to tokenizer byte-pair encodings. - Synthetic generation cannot anticipate all proprietary API token structures. - Running a 500M model forward pass on every raw configuration file wastes compute.

EdgeSLM implements a Tier-1 Deterministic Secret Scanner (src/inference/policy.py) that acts as a fast, infallible zero-latency firewall.

docs.title: Supported Credential Formats
docs.text:
The Tier-1 scanner runs in \(< 1\text{ ms}\) and detects:

Credential Class Pattern Specification Examples Caught Cryptographic Keys Structural PEM & OpenSSH blocks -----BEGIN RSA PRIVATE KEY-----, -----BEGIN OPENSSH PRIVATE KEY----- Cloud Provider Keys AWS Access Key IDs & Session Tokens AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}, ASIA... Developer Platforms GitHub Personal Access Tokens ghp_[A-Za-z0-9_]{36,255}, gho_... Enterprise SaaS Slack Bot & User Tokens xoxb-[0-9]{11,13}-[0-9]{11,13}-[a-zA-Z0-9]{24} Financial / Payments Stripe Live Secret Keys sk_live_[0-9a-zA-Z]{24} Database URIs Connection strings with credentials postgres://user:pass@host:5432/db, mongodb+srv://..., redis://...

docs.title: Performance & Real-World Validation
docs.text:
On the 100-document enterprise benchmark (real-bench-100): - Live Secret Recall: 100% (15 out of 15 keys caught) - Mean Scanner Latency: 0.42 ms - Zero Cloud Leakage: Evaluated entirely on local CPU buffers.

When a Tier-1 secret is detected, EdgeSLM immediately returns RESTRICTED with "policy_override": true, bypassing the neural network forward pass entirely.

docs.title: Dynamic Tensor Chunk Batching 🚀
docs.text: Real-world enterprise documents (such as board meeting minutes, legal vendor agreements, and engineering handbooks) often span multiple pages, resulting in anywhere from 2 to 25 token chunks.

docs.title: The Sequential Processing Bottleneck
docs.text:
In naive document classifiers, long documents are evaluated chunk-by-chunk in a sequential Python loop:

# Naive sequential loop
chunk_scores = []
for chunk in document_chunks:
    scores = model.classify(chunk)  # Launches separate CUDA kernel each chunk!
    chunk_scores.append(scores)

This sequential pattern causes severe GPU underutilization: 1. Kernel Launch Overhead: Launching separate PyTorch forward passes sequentially pays host-to-device synchronization latency on every chunk. 2. Memory Bandwidth Waste: For each chunk, model parameters are loaded repeatedly from VRAM, keeping arithmetic intensity low. 3. High Latency: An 8-chunk document takes \(\approx 1.5\text{ seconds}\) to process sequentially.

docs.title: The Dynamic Tensor Batching Solution
docs.text:
EdgeSLM implements Dynamic Tensor Batching (src/inference/classifier.py): - All text chunks of a multi-page document are tokenized and dynamically padded to the batch's longest chunk. - An attention mask (\(B \times L\)) ensures padded tokens do not influence attention projections. - The entire document is evaluated in a single batched forward pass through the SLM's transformer layers.

Multi-Page Document (e.g. 8 Chunks)
┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐ ┌────────┐
│ Chunk 1│ │ Chunk 2│ │ Chunk 3│ │ Chunk 4│ │ Chunk 5│ │ Chunk 6│ │ Chunk 7│ │ Chunk 8│
└────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘ └────┬───┘
     │          │          │          │          │          │          │          │
     └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┴─────┬────┴──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘
                                            ▼
                           Dynamic Tensor Batch [8, Seq_Len]
                                            │
                                            ▼
                        Single Parallel Transformer Kernel (CUDA)
                                            │
                                            ▼
                           Class Probabilities [8, 4 Classes]

docs.title: Empirical Benchmark Results (RTX 3050 GPU)
docs.text:
Measured using src/edge/benchmark_inference.py across varying document lengths:

Document Chunks Sequential Loop Latency Dynamic Batching Latency Speedup Factor Throughput (Chunks/sec) Latency Saved 1 Chunk 166.0 ms 157.4 ms 1.05x 6.4 chunks/s 5.2% 2 Chunks 396.0 ms 183.8 ms 2.15x 10.9 chunks/s 53.6% 4 Chunks 684.3 ms 245.3 ms 2.79x 16.3 chunks/s 64.2% 8 Chunks 1,497.5 ms 223.7 ms 6.69x 35.8 chunks/s 85.1%

Multi-chunk document latency plummets from 1.5 seconds down to 223 ms—a 6.69x speedup on consumer hardware with zero accuracy degradation.

docs.title: ONNX 4-Bit Edge Quantization 🗜️
docs.text: To run edge inference on consumer laptops without discrete GPUs, EdgeSLM exports trained LoRA adapters to ONNX Runtime and evaluates multiple quantization strategies.

docs.title: The Edge Quantization Dilemma: INT8 vs. 4-Bit
docs.text: In early experiments with SmolLM2-360M, standard dynamic INT8 quantization caused catastrophic accuracy degradation on contrastive sets.

docs.title: The INT8 Diagnostic
docs.text: Profiling revealed that dynamic INT8 quantizes both weights and activations: - In small language models (\(\le 500\text{M}\) parameters), activation tensors exhibit high dynamic range outliers. - Quantizing activations to 8-bit integers distorted the logit distributions of single label tokens. - Solution: Switch to weight-only quantization. Keeping activations in floating point (FP32/FP16) while compressing weights preserves numerical fidelity.

docs.title: 4-Bit Quantization on Qwen2.5-0.5B
docs.text:
Using ONNX block-wise 4-bit weight quantization:

Build Variant Model Size RAM Usage Laptop CPU Latency (Ryzen 5) Contrast Accuracy (95% Wilson) PyTorch FP32 Baseline 1,890 MB 2,450 MB 1,420 ms 88.8% [80–94] ONNX FP32 1,870 MB 2,120 MB 1,180 ms 88.8% [80–94] ONNX 4-Bit Weight-Only 392 MB 1,040 MB 520 ms 88.8% [80–94]

docs.title: Statistical Verification: Zero Accuracy Loss
docs.text:
Paired exact McNemar tests confirm that the 4-bit ONNX edge build matches full precision FP32 across all evaluation sets (\(p \ge 0.5\)).

4-bit compression reduced model size by 79.2% and cut CPU inference latency by 2.7x with zero statistical loss in accuracy.

docs.title: Exporting the Model
docs.text:
To export and quantize your own fine-tuned adapter:

uv run python src/edge/export_onnx.py \
  --adapter experiments/qwen0.5b-v2 \
  --output experiments/edge-qwen \
  --variants onnx-int4-weight-only

docs.title: Speculative Early-Exit ⏩
docs.text:
In enterprise Data Loss Prevention (DLP), documents are classified hierarchically: a document inherits the label of its most sensitive chunk. Therefore, if a document contains an NDA clause or production credentials on page 1, classifying the remaining 20 pages cannot lower the document's classification tier.

EdgeSLM leverages this structural invariant with Speculative Early-Exit.

docs.title: Early-Exit Mechanism
docs.text:
When scanning multi-page documents: 1. EdgeSLM evaluates the first chunk (or an initial batch). 2. If the predicted label is high-severity (RESTRICTED or CONFIDENTIAL) with confidence exceeding the threshold: $\(P(\text{label}) \ge 0.98\)$ 3. Inference terminates immediately. The remaining chunks are skipped, and the document is classified at maximum sensitivity.

Document Ingestion
       │
       ▼
[ Chunk 1 ] ──► P(CONFIDENTIAL) = 0.998  ──(Confidence >= 0.98)──► HALT INFERENCE!
       │                                                          Label: CONFIDENTIAL
   [ Chunk 2 ]   (SKIPPED - 0 ms)
   [ Chunk 3 ]   (SKIPPED - 0 ms)
   [ Chunk 4 ]   (SKIPPED - 0 ms)
   ...
   [ Chunk 9 ]   (SKIPPED - 0 ms)

docs.title: Quantitative Savings
docs.text:
Evaluated on multi-page sensitive enterprise contracts:

Metric Sequential Scan (All Chunks) Speculative Early-Exit Efficiency Gain Chunks Processed 9 chunks 1 chunk 88.9% compute reduction Inference Latency 1,227 ms 243 ms 80.2% latency reduction Classification Accuracy 100% 100% (Identical) Zero accuracy loss

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
In src/inference/classifier.py and the FastAPI service, early-exit can be toggled:

# Enable speculative early-exit for high-throughput batch scanning
result = classifier.classify_document(
    document_text,
    early_exit=True,
    early_exit_threshold=0.98
)
